--- a/minbpe/_rare.py
+++ b/minbpe/_rare.py
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+"""
+Helpers only needed on uncommon paths (very long merge inputs, token ids that
+do not fit in one code point). Kept in their own module so that importing
+minbpe does not have to compile them.
+"""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as base.apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list
+    over the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for
+    every mergeable adjacent pair. Entries are validated lazily when popped,
+    and each round pops all entries of the minimal rank in position order. The
+    first valid one picks the pair (same as the first-seen minimal pair); its
+    occurrences are merged left to right, skipping overlaps, like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+
+
+def _update_stats(stats, old, new, pair, idx):
+    """
+    Update pair counts (stats of old) in place so they become the stats of new,
+    where new = merge(old, pair, idx) and idx does not occur in old. Only pairs
+    touching a merged occurrence change; zero counts are removed.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    get = stats.get
+    n_old = len(old)
+    k = new.count(idx)
+    index = new.index
+    removed = [pair]
+    rapp = removed.append
+    added = set() # pairs whose count went up
+    aadd = added.add
+    prev = -2
+    q = -1
+    for m in range(k):
+        q = index(idx, q + 1)
+        j = q + m # position of this occurrence in old
+        if q and prev != q - 1:
+            # left neighbour is untouched (an adjacent previous occurrence
+            # already accounted for the pair between them)
+            a = new[q-1]
+            p = (a, p0)
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            p = (a, idx)
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+            aadd(p)
+        if j + 2 < n_old:
+            p = (p1, old[j+2])
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            p = (idx, new[q+1])
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+            aadd(p)
+        prev = q
+    stats[pair] -= k
+    for p in removed:
+        if get(p) == 0:
+            del stats[p]
+    return added
+

journal.text:
I read the minbpe lineage end to end: lineage_bench.py, regex.py, base.py, basic.py, gpt4.py and __init__.py. I also searched for import sites of minbpe, which turned up 13 matching lines. Then I wrote a new file, minbpe/_rare.py, at 117 lines. My plan was to move a rarely used path out of the main tokenizer code.

What happened is less than that. I never wired _rare.py into anything, I ran no sandbox evaluations, and the session stopped with no candidate submitted. I have no measured result of any kind.

What I believe now is that the bench drives the code through base.py, basic.py and regex.py. The 13 import lines are where any refactor would have to stay compatible. Adding a file on its own changes nothing the bench measures.

Next time I should run the bench first to get a baseline. After that I can either connect _rare.py to a real call site in regex.py or basic.py and measure, or delete it. I should only submit once a sandbox run shows a difference.
